newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares slip to negative ground.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares slip to negative ground.

text.p: Wall Street shares slipped to negative ground in morning trading on Thursday, as a stream of economic data sent mixed signals ahead of a key employment report due out tomorrow.
Stocks and bonds initially rose after the release of second quarter gross domestic product data which showed an annualized rise of 2.2 percent and a very small gain in the price deflator.
But bonds edged off highs and stocks followed suit after the Chicago Purchasing Managers data for July.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was down 28 points at 8226 and the Nasdaq composite lost 0.88 points to 1587.
The long bond, whose declining yields sent stocks soaring yesterday, pulled off highs to trade up 6/32 at 6.32 percent.

"The GDP data that came out this morning was very market-friendly but the prices paid component of the Chicago PMI brought a little concern into the market," Charles White, managing director of Avatar Associates, said.
The Chicago PMI read 60.6 in July versus a 61.5 reading in June but the prices paid component rose to 61.6 from 53.7.
